metadata.case_name: KWOK HOI WAN IRENE ALSO KNOWN AS GUO HAIYUN SUING BY HER HUSBAND AND NEXT FRIEND CHENG YUK CHING v. THE HOSPITAL AUTHORITY

plaintiff.occupation_before: Sales and executive manager in a trading firm; engaged to work at the Zhuhai City office as sales and executive manager assisting with sales and administrative matters of the business.

injuries.description: Severe hypoxic brain damage / hypoxic encephalopathy (persistent vegetative state / minimally conscious state).
source: periods of hypotension and severe anaemia during which the plaintiff was likely to have suffered from hypoxic brain damage.

injuries.description: Severe anaemia and periods of hypotension associated with difficulty in cross-matching of blood.
source: Difficulty encountered in cross-matching of blood resulted in periods of hypotension and severe anaemia during which the plaintiff was likely to have suffered from hypoxic brain damage.

manifestations.description: The plaintiff has suffered severely impaired higher mental functions with no consistent response to verbal stimuli.
She does not turn her head when spoken to but responds to the sour taste of lemon by licking her lips.
She is attentive to tactile stimulus when her hair is brushed.
There is spontaneous eye opening and visual tracking of light.
She is startled by sudden loud noises but such response occurred in less than 5% of trials.
The plaintiff is totally uncommunicative but sometimes would utter unintelligible sounds.
She is unable to swallow and has to be fed by nasogastric tube. When orally fed, she chokes.
There is no spontaneous movement in her limbs although she sometimes raises her arms when yawning.
She is bedridden and unable to sit in a wheelchair owing to poor neck and trunk control or turn in bed.
Being doubly incontinent, she is completely dependent as regards feeding, bathing, dressing and toileting.
There was no response in eye, head or limb movement upon request.
The plaintiff has lost all capacity for work.
The plaintiff's neurological status lies somewhere between the persistent vegetative state ("PVS") and minimally conscious state ("MCS").

losses.description: This is plainly a "disaster" case ... it cannot be doubted that the plaintiff will require constant care and attention for the remainder of her compromised life and is incapable of ever leading or appreciating an independent existence.
The plaintiff is totally uncommunicative but sometimes would utter unintelligible sounds.

losses.category: Loss of ability to do domestic tasks
losses.description: Being doubly incontinent, she is completely dependent as regards feeding, bathing, dressing and toileting.
She is bedridden and unable to sit in a wheelchair owing to poor neck and trunk control or turn in bed.
The plaintiff has lost all capacity for work.
Damages for loss of the plaintiff’s society under s 20C(1) of the Law Amendment and Reform (Consolidation) Ordinance, Cap 23 are agreed at $150,000.

Both neurologists are in agreement that the life expectancy of patients in a state of PVS and MCS will be compromised; Dr Huang opined survival to 51.5 years giving realistically a further 14.5 years from age 37.
